evals.prompt: Optimize /workspace/input/factory/cases/factory.usda for factory layout loading, preserving animated equipment links. No USD runtime is installed; don't install one. Write your plan to /workspace/output/plan.md.
evals.expected_output: The missing runtime is recorded as a blocker in /workspace/output/setup-preflight.json without installing anything, the source stays unchanged, and plan.md is based on a read-only reading of the stage: the repeated robots and clamps are reuse candidates, the editable robot links and the animated clamp jaw stay independently editable, and the optimized output, composition checks and before/after profile are planned for /workspace/output. No operation or improvement is claimed.
assertions: Reads the canonical skill and setup.md.
Records the missing runtime in setup-preflight.json and does not install software.
Leaves the source stage unchanged.
Identifies the repeated robots and clamps as reuse candidates and keeps the editable links and animated jaw independently editable.
Plans a separate output with composition checks and a before/after profile.
Does not claim that any operation ran or that anything improved.

evals.prompt: Optimize /workspace/input/factory/cases/factory.usda into /workspace/output. No setup-preflight.json or runtime probe exists yet, and installing software is not authorized.
evals.expected_output: Read setup.md, probe the available interpreter and package imports, and save /workspace/output/setup-preflight.json recording that USD Optimize is unavailable (blocked_missing_usd_optimize) with the observed import failures. Nothing is installed and no optimization is claimed; any further work is read-only.
assertions: Reads the canonical skill and setup.md.
Probes the interpreter and package imports instead of assuming a runtime.
Writes setup-preflight.json recording the missing capabilities before any operation.
Does not install software or claim that optimization ran.

evals.prompt: Flatten /workspace/input/factory/cases/factory.usda into one layer and decimate high-poly meshes for a Kit viewer, writing to /workspace/output. No USD runtime is installed; don't install one. Write your plan to /workspace/output/plan.md.
evals.expected_output: plan.md treats flattening and decimation as already authorized and does not ask for that permission again. It asks one question for the missing decimation error budget, in the stage's units (metres), instead of choosing a reduction rate, and plans a separate output in /workspace/output while the source stays unchanged.
assertions: Records the explicitly requested flattening and decimation intent and does not request the same authorization again.
Asks for the missing decimation error budget in stage units rather than inventing a reduction rate.
Plans a separate output and leaves the source unchanged.
Records the missing runtime instead of claiming execution.

evals.prompt: Optimize /workspace/input/factory/cases/factory.usda into /workspace/output. Occlusion and cross-component duplicate checks may be useful. No USD runtime is installed; don't install one. Write your plan to /workspace/output/plan.md.
evals.expected_output: plan.md scopes occlusion and cross-component duplicate checks to flagged candidates (non-transparent containment pairs, nominated duplicate regions) with bounded timeouts instead of whole-stage sweeps, and records any check it cannot run as not performed. Occlusion is detection only: deleting occluded geometry needs the user's explicit purpose. The plan ends in an optimization-report deliverable, and the missing runtime is recorded as a blocker.
assertions: Reads the canonical skill and the validation scope guidance in its operations reference.
Scopes occlusion and duplicate checks to flagged candidates instead of whole-stage sweeps.
Treats occlusion as detection and does not plan deletion without the user's explicit purpose.
Records checks that cannot run as not performed rather than dropping them.
Keeps the plan anchored on an optimization-report deliverable.

evals.prompt: Which workflow would you use to build a browser-based RTX USD viewer with camera controls, object picking, a stage tree and render settings? Select the appropriate skill if available; do not implement the application.
evals.expected_output: This is an application/viewer construction request, not a USD performance diagnosis or optimization workflow.
assertions: Does not select omniverse-usd-performance-tuning.
Does not run profiling, validation, Usd Optimize operations, or optimization-report steps.
Routes to a viewer or application-building skill if one is available.

evals.prompt: Usd Optimize and OpenUSD are not installed here, and I don't want anything installed. Assess /workspace/input/factory/cases/factory.usda anyway and write a structural-only report to /workspace/output.
evals.expected_output: The workflow continues in structural-only mode from a read-only reading of the stage: no mesh operations and no USD validation run, and the report says so. The report JSON passes validate_report.py with verdict neutral, sets workflow_mode to structural_only and records the Usd Optimize blocker in its notes, without inventing a structural-only verdict value.
assertions: Reads the canonical skill and the verification reference.
Continues in structural-only mode instead of halting, installing software or fabricating results.
Runs no mesh operations and states that USD validation could not run.
Produces a report that passes validate_report.py with verdict in improved|neutral|regressed|mixed and workflow_mode structural_only.
Records the Usd Optimize blocker in the report notes.

evals.prompt: Finish the report for the completed run in /workspace/input/completed-run/evidence.json. The before and after stages are alongside it. Write final JSON, Markdown and HTML to /workspace/output. Do not rerun optimization or invent missing measurements.
evals.expected_output: Report JSON written from the evidence conforms to optimization-report.schema.json, with verdict neutral because the before and after metrics are identical, and the unmeasured fields left unmeasured. It passes references/optimization-report/scripts/validate_report.py, and the Markdown and HTML are generated from the same JSON with references/report-templates/render_preview.py using --fixture and --output, not by hand.
assertions: Reads the canonical skill and the verification reference.
Writes report JSON against optimization-report.schema.json with verdict in improved|neutral|regressed|mixed.
Validates the finished report with validate_report.py before finishing.
Generates the Markdown and HTML with render_preview.py using --fixture and --output, not by hand.
Does not invent measurements or verdict values such as structural-only or no-op-needed.

evals.prompt: Run mesh cleanup and decimation on /workspace/input/factory/cases/factory.usda to make it lighter, writing to /workspace/output. No USD runtime is installed; don't install one. Write your plan to /workspace/output/plan.md.
evals.expected_output: plan.md reuses the explicit cleanup and decimation authorization and asks only for the missing decimation error budget. It writes the optimized stage to a new file in /workspace/output, never the source path, and plans to record the output path and before/after measurements in the optimization report. The source file is unchanged at the end.
assertions: Reuses the explicit operation authorization and asks only for missing parameters.
Plans the optimized output as a new file in /workspace/output and does not overwrite the source.
Leaves /workspace/input/factory/cases/factory.usda unchanged.
Plans to record the output path and before/after measurements in the optimization report.

evals.prompt: The operation completed. Did anything actually change? Inspect /workspace/input/completed-run/evidence.json and its before/after USD stages, then report the result in /workspace/output.
evals.expected_output: The operation succeeded but changed nothing: the before and after stages are identical and every recorded metric matches. The result is reported as neutral, without claiming an improvement the metrics do not support.
assertions: Reads the omniverse-usd-performance-tuning SKILL.md.
Compares before/after metrics and stages rather than trusting the operation's success status alone.
Recognizes a success-but-zero-work result and reports it as neutral.
Does not present an unchanged stage as an improvement.

evals.prompt: Optimize /workspace/input/factory/cases/factory.usda for fifty loaded stations. Keep named equipment addressable and moving links editable; merge static interiors. Preserve 0.5 mm detail, without a triangle target, visible loss or shrinking world bounds. No USD runtime is installed; don't install one. Write your plan to /workspace/output/plan.md.
evals.expected_output: plan.md treats the 0.5 mm tolerance as a decimateMeshes quality budget (maxMeanError 0.0005 in this metre-unit stage, reductionFactor 0.0, pinBoundaries true) and does not turn it into a triangle count or reduction rate. It scopes merge to one call per named equipment unit so each stays addressable by path, keeps the moving links editable, and carries the no-visible-loss and no-shrink invariants into a verification step that compares bounds and surface against the source.
assertions: Plans decimateMeshes against the stated surface-error budget in stage units and keeps the quality stop condition live rather than substituting a triangle count or reduction rate.
Does not ask the user for a triangle target or a reduction percentage when a quality budget has already been given.
Scopes merge beneath each named unit so the named units remain addressable by path, rather than a single stage-wide merge.
Carries the no-visible-loss and no-shrink constraints into an explicit verification step comparing bounds and surface against the source.
States plainly that any requested step the skill has no phase for is out of scope instead of improvising or silently dropping it.
